notes: Converted from MAME's src/mame/atari/nl_flyball.cpp (NETLIST_START(flyball), CC0-1.0, Ryan Holtz) at mame0289 by tools/mame_netlist.py. Every change from MAME's file -- the simulation stand-ins undone, the hacks dropped, the corrections from the sheet -- is logged at the top of boards/flyball-sound.nets.

Compared with the schematic, sheet 7 of 9 'Sound Generator' (005629 rev A, TM-075 pp. 56-57, the sheet scanned in two halves), with parts list A005629-01 (pp. 62-65), on 2026-10-20: 39 of MAME's 41 nets agree pin for pin -- the noise generator (all ten of its connections), the band-pass filter, the bat sound's 556, the footstep envelope, the crowd and whistle control and the mixer -- and the supplies are as MAME has them (+18V, an unregulated rail, on A8, C8 and D8). Corrected above from the sheet: D7.1, E7.2 and E7.13 go to +5V through the 1K pull-up R25, which MAME leaves out, and B7 and C7 pins 2 and 9 (B gate and CLR) are drawn as bare stubs, which MAME ties to +5V -- an open TTL input floats high, the level the circuit needs, so the board may tie them, but the drawing does not. D7.13 is drawn 'P', an unnamed pull-up, and is left on +5V here.

Kept as MAME has them, each against the sheet: R79 is 820K on the sheet and the parts list and 1K in MAME, whose comment says 'Verified as 1K on a real board'; R97B (24.4K, in parallel with R97) is on neither, and MAME's comment says it was 'verified to exist on a real board'; C46/C47 are .01 on the sheet and .015 on the parts list, which MAME follows; R80 is 330K on the sheet and 330 ohms on the parts list, and MAME follows the sheet. A8 and C8 are printed 'MFC3340P' with the MFC6040's pin numbers in brackets beside each pin, and the parts list fits MFC6040s, with the MFC3340 as the substitute 'when stock of MFC6040 is depleted'; this file is the MFC3340 wiring, so a board carrying MFC6040s has the bracketed pins instead (as Tank's do). E7's fourth gate (4, 5, 6), which MAME grounds, is not on sheet 7, and the output amplifier (the TDA1004 at B9) is on it and not in MAME.
